page.layout: One column of alphabetical index entries, with page numbers printed beneath some entries and set to the right; the right-hand part of the column runs off the scan edge.; One column of index entries, numbers in the right-hand part of the column. Left edges are cut, so some entries begin with word fragments. Index letters "I" and "N" at the top.; One column of index entries, running down the page; a large "V" section heading with "Ac" in the middle, and the running letters "D E" at the top.; One column of index entries on the right of the scan, set in alphabetical order by letter with page numbers flush right. Left parts of the lines are cut off. Letters V and X are section headers.
page.notes: The scan is cut at the right edge, so entries and page numbers running beyond the visible edge are not shown. The first line "tripertiri" and the entries "triplicare" and similar are transcribed as printed; "tristem esse" and "truncus succisus" are read as printed with long s rendered as s. Left-edge word fragments ("a", "o", "rbo") are kept as they appear. The word beginning "ultyatio" is unclear and is marked [?]. The last entry line of the strip may be incomplete. Several entries are cut off at the right edge of the strip (turmati, turpitue, turpitua, turris, valedic, validum, validus, vanum); they are transcribed as far as they are visible. The reading "tusio" for "tufio" and the page reference "60" under "vaci" are doubtful. The "VAc" heading is a large initial V with small "Ac" beside it. Left edges of many lines are cut off, so the first words of several entries are missing or partly visible; the transcription keeps only what shows. Lines marked with "..." or fragments such as "66", "659" and "369" show only their right part. The entry "tympanistriæ, tym-" is a hyphenated line break, and the printed long s is written as plain s.
